topic_tag: mountain monastery's role between two valleys
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In a history of the pass, one scholar described the monastery as, above all, the region's ______.

worlds.passage: For six centuries a small monastery stood at the top of the only pass between two mountain valleys, each ruled by its own lord. Each lord's soldiers held his own end of the road, and neither lord trusted the other's toll keepers. Every cart that came up the pass stopped at the monastery gate, where the monks listed its load and sealed it with the abbot's stamp, refusing the seal to any cart carrying weapons. Toll keepers in both valleys waved sealed carts through and searched any other to the last sack. In a history of the pass, one scholar described the monastery as, above all, the region's ______.
worlds.explanation: Neither valley trusted the other's searches, and both let through only the carts the monks had examined and sealed, so the monastery was where traffic was inspected: the region's "checkpoint." "Broker" fails because the monks examine loads and arrange no dealings between the lords; "custodian" fails because the road is guarded by the lords' own soldiers and every cart moves on, so the monks keep and guard nothing; "counterweight" fails because the monastery serves both valleys alike rather than offsetting either lord's power.

broker.quote: listed its load and sealed it
broker.why: The monks' work is examining cargo, not carrying offers or arranging terms between the lords.

custodian.quote: Each lord's soldiers held his own end
custodian.why: Guarding the road belongs to the lords' soldiers, and the carts pass on; the monastery keeps nothing in its care.

counterweight.why: Both valleys rely on the seal equally; the monastery balances no one's power against another's.

worlds.passage: For six centuries a small monastery stood at the top of the only pass between two mountain valleys, each ruled by its own lord. The lords spoke different languages and, after a long war, would let none of each other's envoys into their valleys. Monks who knew both tongues carried each lord's offers over the pass and back, proposed terms on grazing rights and on marriages between the two houses, and saw the treaties that kept the peace for two centuries drafted in the monastery's hall. In a history of the pass, one scholar described the monastery as, above all, the region's ______.
worlds.explanation: Two parties who will not meet reach agreements through monks who carry their offers and propose the terms, so the monastery is the region's "broker." "Checkpoint" fails because the monks cross the pass with messages; no traveler is stopped or examined; "custodian" fails because the monastery shapes agreements rather than keeping anything safe; "counterweight" fails because it sides with neither lord but brings the two together.

checkpoint.quote: carried each lord's offers over the pass
checkpoint.why: The monks themselves travel back and forth with messages; the passage describes no inspection of anyone crossing.

custodian.why: The monks' work is arranging terms between parties, not holding or protecting anything on someone's behalf.

counterweight.why: The monastery joins the two sides in agreements; it is not a power set against one of them.

worlds.passage: For six centuries a small monastery stood at the top of the only pass between two mountain valleys, each ruled by its own lord. When raiders burned the lowland towns, families from both valleys carried their deeds, seed grain, and church silver up to the monastery, whose walls the raiders never breached. The monks sealed each family's goods in the vaults under its name and handed them back when the family returned, sometimes a generation later, with the seals unbroken. In a history of the pass, one scholar described the monastery as, above all, the region's ______.
worlds.explanation: Families leave their most valuable property with the monks, who hold it under seal for as long as needed and return it intact, so the monastery is the region's "custodian." "Checkpoint" fails because the families climb up to the monastery to leave goods, not to cross; nothing is examined; "broker" fails because no dealings between parties are arranged; "counterweight" fails because the raiders are kept out by walls, not offset by a rival power, and the lords play no part.

checkpoint.quote: carried their deeds, seed grain, and church silver up
checkpoint.why: The families bring goods up to leave them, not to pass through, and no one is examined or admitted.

broker.quote: handed them back when the family returned
broker.why: The goods go back to their own owners; the monks arrange no exchange or agreement between two sides.

counterweight.quote: whose walls the raiders never breached
counterweight.why: The protection is the safety of what is stored, not a balance struck against any lord's or raider's power.

worlds.passage: For six centuries a small monastery stood at the top of the only pass between two mountain valleys, each ruled by its own lord. In time the eastern lord grew rich enough to want the western valley's pastures as well. The monastery owned half the high grazing land, its abbots were elected by western villages, and the bishop sided with the abbots in every dispute, so for two centuries the eastern lord never had enough land, men, or church support to take the pastures he wanted. In a history of the pass, one scholar described the monastery as, above all, the region's ______.
worlds.explanation: A growing eastern power is held level by the monastery's own weight in land, local loyalty, and church backing, so the monastery is the region's "counterweight." "Checkpoint" fails because the eastern lord is held back by the balance of land and allies, not by inspection at a gate; "broker" fails because the monastery takes one side's part in every dispute rather than arranging terms; "custodian" fails because the monastery holds its own land in its own interest, not anyone's property in trust.

checkpoint.quote: never had enough land, men, or church support
checkpoint.why: What stops the eastern lord is the balance of resources, not a gate where people are examined.

broker.quote: the bishop sided with the abbots in every dispute
broker.why: The monastery is a party in each dispute, backed by the bishop, not a go-between arranging terms.

custodian.quote: monastery owned half the high grazing land
custodian.why: The land is the monastery's own; it is not holding anyone else's property in safekeeping.
